correctness.rationale: For every distinct primes p<q, the r selected positive entries preceding p in an addition chain are distinct nonidentity residues mod p; recursive atomic R(a_j,a_k,a_i) equalities force all q-side choices to be a_i*y. Closing the chain with R(a_j,a_k,e) forces p*y=0. Since q is prime distinct from p, y=0, contradicting the named identity relation on the first move. For p+1, either truncate at a preceding p or close with R(a_j,a_k,a_0), forcing (p+1)y=y. For p-1, select the endpoint (r+1 moves) and close (p-1)y+y=0. Yao’s singleton power-evaluation bound yields l(p)<=log2(p)+O(log p/loglog p), thus n+O(n/log n) where 2^n<p<2^(n+1). Explicit small-chain arithmetic and closure cases were independently reconstructed from actual verify.py, which tests only finite instances and is not the universal proof.
